set.body:
THE SINGLE MISSING TRANSFORMATION IN THE END-TO-END PATH: SurfaceAtlas -> NarrativeGraph +
NarrativeHierarchy. Nothing produces them. Not an implementation, not a stub, not a provider trait.

ESTABLISHED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, FROM OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS:
  - claude-storymodel4s-m1 traced it from the BUILD GRAPH.
  - codex-storymodel-research-spike walked into it from RAW TEXT, blind -- I deliberately withheld
    m1's location and asked it to report where IT stopped. It stopped at the same joint.

BOTH ENDS ALREADY RUN. Transcript -> RecallGraph is two function calls. SourceView ->
RecallSignature is four lines with library defaults. The pipeline is not missing; it is severed at
one point.

AND THE MODULE NAMED FOR IT STRUCTURALLY CANNOT DO IT. Re-verified against build.sbt at 16:43Z:

    lazy val acquire = crossProject(...).dependsOn(core, proposition)

NO DEPENDENCY ON `story`. So `acquire` CANNOT NAME THE TYPE IT WOULD HAVE TO RETURN --
`NarrativeHierarchy` appears zero times in acquire/src, and in codec, fixtures, laws and story
everywhere else. Additionally: no module outside acquire imports `storymodel4s.acquire` in main
sources, despite seven declaring the dependency; and `TaskPacket`, `Resolver.resolve`,
`BuildPlan.from` and `PatchApplier.applyPatch` have no production construction site.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS, and it is m1's wording: the roadmap says all of this honestly --
acquire is M0 "pure" -- but "THE ACQUISITION MODULE EXISTS" and "IT IS UNWIRED AND CANNOT COMPILE
AGAINST ITS OWN OUTPUT TYPE" are different sentences, and only the first has been said aloud.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OPEN ITEM. Two independent state-of-the-state assessments
converged on the same sentence: the project is strong at not lying about what it computed and has
not shown a researcher can use it. This link is the whole of that gap that is an ENGINEERING task
rather than an owner decision. The other half -- no real human data -- is blocked on the owner's PD
sign-off and no amount of code closes it.

SCOPE, and it is NOT "add a build dependency". That understates it and I refused to file it that
way this afternoon for exactly that reason:
  1. Decide WHERE the transformation lives. `acquire` is the module named for it and cannot express
     its output type; making it depend on `story` is one answer and inverting the direction is
     another. This is an architecture question and it wants an ADR, not a build.sbt edit.
  2. The transformation itself is UNATTENDED-BUILD work under design rule 13: agents return typed
     proposals with evidence, only the deterministic resolver creates accepted claims, and
     unresolved outcomes are legitimate artifacts.
  3. It must produce something the existing consumers accept unchanged. Both ends already work; the
     acceptance test is that a raw transcript reaches RecallSignature without a hand-authored model.

NOT SCHEDULING IT AND NOT ASSIGNING IT. It is P1 and it is the largest piece of open work in the
project; it wants an owner with uninterrupted time and probably an ADR first. I am filing it
because I said I would hold it until the spike's blind result and then did not file it when the
result arrived two hours ago -- the most important finding of the day sat untracked while I wrote
rulebook amendments.
set.title: acquire/story: nothing produces NarrativeGraph + NarrativeHierarchy from a SurfaceAtlas - the one severed link in the end-to-end path
